about.title: Santa Rosa Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Santa Rosa takes many shapes: construction crews, warehouse and delivery shifts along Santa Rosa Avenue, agricultural labor at the edge of town, and hospital and hospitality jobs that run around the clock. When one of those days ends in an injury, one question comes up fast: who pays for this? In California, your employer's workers' compensation coverage usually answers that, regardless of who was at fault. It covers medical care and part of your lost wages, but not pain and suffering, and it is generally the only claim you can bring against the employer itself. Many Sonoma County workers don't realize a separate claim may exist when someone other than the employer caused the harm. A subcontractor on the site, the maker of a defective tool, a property owner who ignored a hazard, or another driver who hit your work vehicle on US-101 or Stony Point Road can each be held responsible on their own. LawProactive helps you sort out which path fits, then connects you free with an independent attorney.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Rosa Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We look past the workers' comp ceiling
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it leaves out pain and suffering. The attorneys we connect you with check whether a negligent third party opens a second, fuller claim.

items.title: Timing matters, and we help you stay ahead of it
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and third-party injury claims carry a two-year deadline. Getting connected early keeps both clocks from running out on you.

items.title: Retaliation is illegal, and you shouldn't face it alone
items.desc: Your employer cannot lawfully fire, demote, or punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. An independent attorney can step in if that starts to happen after you speak up.

items.question: I was rear-ended on US-101 while driving a company vehicle in Santa Rosa. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your wages no matter who caused the crash. Because another driver was at fault, you may also have a separate third-party claim against that driver for damages workers' comp doesn't pay, including pain and suffering. Santa Rosa recorded 562 injury collisions in 2025, and a fair number of those involved people simply doing their jobs on the road.

items.question: Do I have to report my injury to my employer, and how quickly?
items.answer: Yes. California asks you to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury, and doing it in writing is the safest approach. Waiting longer can complicate your workers' comp benefits, so report it even if the injury seems minor at first. Reporting is protected activity, and your employer cannot legally retaliate against you for it.

items.question: What does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we simply match you with an independent attorney who handles workplace injury cases. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
